rics.description: Average selling price, all industries, current
rics.meaning: BI Real Sector Business Activity Survey: Average Selling Price, All Industries, Current Period — net balance of firms reporting selling-price increases vs decreases.
rics.how_to_use: Leading indicator of producer-price inflation and CPI goods-component (1-3 month lead). Sustained net positive readings flag pricing-power return; net negative signals competitive deflation. BI watches as inflation-momentum gauge.

rics.description: Average selling price, all industries, future
rics.meaning: BI Real Sector Business Activity Survey: Average Selling Price, All Industries, Future Period — forward-looking pricing intention from firms.
rics.how_to_use: Leads CPI by ~3 months. Most market-relevant inflation-expectation series at the firm level. Used alongside household inflation expectations (aIDCSGENPR6, aIDPREXFR6M) for triangulated forward inflation reads.

rics.description: Business Surveys, capacity utilization, all industries
rics.meaning: Indonesia business survey series: Business Surveys, capacity utilization, all industries. Captures business-sector activity, expectations, or conditions.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia business surveys (BI's SKDU, S&P Global PMI, BPS sectoral surveys) provide forward-looking and current-state diffusion indicators. Net positive readings = expansion. Pair with hard-data complements for triangulated reads.

rics.description: Business activities, agriculture, future
rics.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Agriculture, Future Period — 1-quarter-ahead expectation for agriculture sector. ~13% of GDP, ~28% of employment (low-productivity formal-informal mix).
rics.how_to_use: Weather (El Niño/La Niña), commodity prices (CPO crude palm oil, rubber), and harvest cycles are dominant drivers. Volatile quarterly. Pair with palm-oil futures and rice-price tracking.

rics.description: Business activities, all industries, current
rics.meaning: Bank Indonesia Real Sector Business Activity Survey: All Industries, Current Period — the headline SBT (Saldo Bersih Tertimbang, weighted net balance). Quarterly survey of ~2,500 firms across 9 sectors. Released ~6 weeks after quarter-end.
rics.how_to_use: THE headline BI quarterly business-conditions print. Net balance: % reporting expansion minus % reporting contraction. Above zero = net positive activity. Indonesia SBT typically runs 5-15 in expansion years. Used by BI itself in MPC deliberations and quoted in Monetary Policy Reports. Cross-check against monthly S&P Global PMI for triangulated business-cycle reads.

rics.description: Business activities, all industries, future
rics.meaning: BI Real Sector Business Activity Survey: All Industries, Future Period — forward-looking version of the headline SBT. 1-quarter-ahead expectations from surveyed firms across all sectors.
rics.how_to_use: Leads aIDBSBACTCR (current SBT) by 1 quarter and aIDCGDPYD/A by 2 quarters. Sharp drops below 5 are recession-warning signals — Indonesia hasn't seen this outside crises (1998, 2020). Pair with current SBT — divergence (current high, future falling) signals cycle peak approaching.

rics.description: Business activities, construction, future
rics.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Construction, Future Period — 1-quarter-ahead construction-sector activity expectation. ~11% of GDP, highly cyclical.
rics.how_to_use: Leads construction GVA growth (aIDVADCONS/C) by 1 quarter. Sensitive to BI rate cycle and infrastructure-spending pipeline. Used in tracking property-cycle and government-spending implementation.

rics.description: Business activities, electricity, gas & water, future
rics.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Electricity, Gas & Water, Future Period — utilities sector forward expectation. Small share (~1%) but stable.
rics.how_to_use: Low cyclicality. Tracks PLN (state electricity utility) and gas-distribution activity. Useful for cross-validating broader business-conditions trends.

rics.description: Business activities, finance, leasing and business services, future
rics.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Finance, Leasing and Business Services, Future Period — financial-sector forward expectation. ~4% of GDP.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks financialization of the economy. Bank profitability cycles, capital-markets activity (IDX trading volume), and insurance sector growth drive this. Watch alongside JCI for financial-sector cycle.

rics.description: Business activities, manufacturing industry, future
rics.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Manufacturing Industry, Future Period — 1-quarter-ahead manufacturing-sector activity expectation. Indonesia's largest sector at ~20% of GDP.
rics.how_to_use: Leads manufacturing GVA growth (aIDVADGM/C) by 1 quarter. Pair with S&P Global Manufacturing PMI (aIDPMIT/A) — when both move in same direction, signal is robust; divergences are usually resolved within 1-2 months.

rics.description: Business activities, mining and quarrying, future
rics.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Mining and Quarrying, Future Period — 1-quarter-ahead expectation for the highly cyclical mining sector. ~10% of GDP, highly correlated with global commodity prices.
rics.how_to_use: Sensitive to global coal/nickel/oil/palm-oil prices. Leads mining GVA growth (aIDVADMIN/C). Combined with commodity-price moves, the most reliable Indonesia sector-cycle leading indicator.

rics.description: Business activities, services, future
rics.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Services Sector, Future Period — 1-quarter-ahead services-sector activity expectation. Services are ~45% of Indonesia GDP.
rics.how_to_use: Largest single sector in expectations. Coincides with services GVA growth. Less cyclical than manufacturing/construction but still meaningful for total-GDP tracking.

rics.description: Business activities, trade, hotel and restaurant, future
rics.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Trade, Hotel and Restaurant, Future Period — distributive-trades and hospitality-sector forward expectation.
rics.how_to_use: Best leading indicator for retail sales (aIDRSLSAR) and tourism-related GVA. Lebaran-Eid timing significantly affects this series — adjust for that when comparing across years.

rics.description: Business activities, transportation and communication, future
rics.meaning: BI Business Activity Survey: Transportation and Communication, Future Period — transport + telecom sector forward expectation. ~10% of GDP.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks logistics demand (cargo, passenger transport) and telecom-sector growth. Indonesia's archipelagic geography makes transport critical; logistics-cost reduction is a long-running policy theme.

rics.description: The usage of labor, all industries, current
rics.meaning: BI Real Sector Business Activity Survey: The Usage of Labor, All Industries, Current Period — net balance of firms reporting labor-usage increases vs decreases.
rics.how_to_use: Leading labor-market indicator at firm level. Coincides with formal-sector employment (aIDCEMFO/A) but releases earlier (BPS Sakernas only biannual). Sustained sub-zero readings flag formal-employment contraction ahead of BPS confirmation.

rics.description: The usage of labor, all industries, future
rics.meaning: BI Real Sector Business Activity Survey: The Usage of Labor, All Industries, Future Period — forward-looking firm-level hiring intentions.
rics.how_to_use: Leads formal employment by 1-2 quarters. Among the most reliable Indonesia labor-market leading indicators given Sakernas's biannual frequency. Sub-zero with current SBT also sub-zero is a strong recession-leading signal.

rics.description: ESG, Global sustainable gap compared to reported GDP

rics.how_to_use: Indonesia's sustainability gap reflects resource-extraction-driven growth. Wider gaps signal greater unsustainability. Watch alongside emissions trajectory (aIDESECOP) and deforestation metrics for total environmental-cost picture.

rics.description: Manufacturing, Industrial confidence indicator
rics.meaning: Indonesia manufacturing-related series: Manufacturing, Industrial confidence indicator. Sectoral indicator covering manufacturing activity dimensions.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside the headline PMI (composite of S&P Global aIDPMI series) and BPS Industrial Production for triangulated manufacturing-cycle reads.

rics.description: Manufacturing Sector, S&P Global PMI, Manufacturing
rics.meaning: Indonesia manufacturing-related series: Manufacturing Sector, S&P Global PMI, Manufacturing. Sectoral indicator covering manufacturing activity dimensions.
rics.how_to_use: Use alongside the headline PMI (composite of S&P Global aIDPMI series) and BPS Industrial Production for triangulated manufacturing-cycle reads.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Backlogs of work
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Backlogs of Work sub-index. Above 50 = backlogs rising; below 50 = backlogs falling.
rics.how_to_use: Rising backlogs signal capacity-stretched producers (positive for output near-term but with risk of lost orders). Falling backlogs may signal weakening demand or improved efficiency. Pair with New Orders to distinguish.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Backlogs of work, SA
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Backlogs of Work sub-index, seasonally adjusted.
rics.how_to_use: Useful for distinguishing capacity-stretched vs demand-weakening regimes. Sustained sub-50 with falling New Orders confirms demand weakness; with stable New Orders suggests efficiency gains.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Empl
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Employment sub-index. Tracks net hiring vs layoff intentions at surveyed manufacturers.
rics.how_to_use: Leads formal manufacturing employment (aIDEMPMF) by 1-2 months. Indonesian manufacturers often delay layoffs (rigid labor laws) so sub-50 sustained signals labor-market deterioration ahead of BPS Sakernas reporting.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Empl, SA
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Employment sub-index, seasonally adjusted — SA version of manufacturing-jobs sentiment.
rics.how_to_use: Smoothed monthly employment-momentum signal. Indonesia's structural under-50 readings 2014-2017 (post-commodity-bust deindustrialization) reverted in 2018+ as manufacturing recovered.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Future Output
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Future Output sub-index. 12-month-forward output expectation from manufacturers.
rics.how_to_use: Most forward-looking PMI sub-component. Sustained drops signal sentiment deterioration ahead of orders/output sub-indices weakening. Indonesia's future-output index typically runs >60 (chronically optimistic) — sustained sub-55 readings are warning signals.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Input prc
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Input Prices sub-index. Tracks changes in costs of materials, labor, energy paid by manufacturers.
rics.how_to_use: Leading indicator for goods CPI and PPI inflation by 1-3 months. Sensitive to global commodity prices and IDR — sharp jumps signal upcoming pass-through to consumer prices. BI watches this for cost-push inflation signals.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Input prc, SA
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Input Prices sub-index, seasonally adjusted — SA cost-pressure gauge.
rics.how_to_use: Indonesia's input-price index typically runs 55-60 (chronic mild input inflation). Spikes above 65 historically follow oil-price surges and IDR weakness — pre-cursor to faster CPI prints 1-2 quarters later.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, New exp orders
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: New Export Orders sub-index. Tracks foreign demand for Indonesian manufactured goods.
rics.how_to_use: Sensitive to global PMI, China industrial activity, and CNY/IDR cross-rate. Diverges from total New Orders — when total holds but exports drop, domestic demand is the support; when exports hold but total drops, domestic weakness emerging.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, New exp orders, SA
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia New Export Orders sub-index, seasonally adjusted.
rics.how_to_use: Tracks ASEAN-export cycle and China-demand cycle. Indonesia's export PMI sub-index has been more volatile than total New Orders post-2020 due to commodity-price-driven China demand swings.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, New orders
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: New Orders sub-index. Captures month-on-month change in new business received by Indonesian manufacturers from domestic and foreign customers.
rics.how_to_use: Most-watched leading sub-index — leads headline PMI by 1-3 months at turning points and leads industrial-production growth (aIDCINDYG/CA) by 2-4 months. Sustained drops below 50 alongside falling output sub-index signal genuine demand weakness vs supply constraints.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, New orders, SA
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia New Orders sub-index, seasonally adjusted — SA version of the leading PMI sub-component. Smooths Lebaran/CNY distortions in the orders pulse.
rics.how_to_use: Best high-frequency forward-looking read on Indonesian manufacturing demand. Watch the spread vs Output sub-index — when New Orders < Output for sustained periods, it signals upcoming production cuts as backlogs run down.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Output
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Output sub-index. Direct measure of changes in production volumes at Indonesian manufacturers.
rics.how_to_use: Coincides with manufacturing GVA growth (aIDVADGM/C) — best cross-check of BPS Industrial Production Index (aIDCINDYG/CA) which has small-sample noise. Sustained sub-50 confirms manufacturing recession.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Output prc
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Output Prices sub-index. Tracks pricing power — whether manufacturers are passing input costs through to selling prices.
rics.how_to_use: Watch the spread vs Input Prices: when input prices rise faster than output prices, manufacturer margins are compressing (corporate-earnings risk). When output prices rise faster, demand is strong enough to support pass-through (inflation risk).

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Output prc, SA
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Output Prices sub-index, seasonally adjusted — SA pricing-power gauge.
rics.how_to_use: Cleanest signal of manufacturer pricing power. Sustained reading near 50 with elevated input prices = margin squeeze; >55 with elevated input = strong pass-through (often signals demand strength).

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Output, SA
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Output sub-index, seasonally adjusted — SA version of the production-volume gauge.
rics.how_to_use: Use for monthly tracking; Lebaran-month distortions are removed. Drop below 50 sustained for 3+ months has historically aligned with quarterly manufacturing GVA contraction.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Quantity of prchs
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Quantity of Purchases sub-index. Tracks input-side purchasing activity (volume of materials bought).
rics.how_to_use: Active purchasing signals manufacturers gearing up for output. Sustained drops align with output cuts. Pair with Stocks of Purchases for full input-cycle picture.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Quantity of prchs, SA
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Quantity of Purchases sub-index, seasonally adjusted.
rics.how_to_use: Smoothed manufacturer purchasing-activity gauge. Useful as raw-material-import predictor (aIDIMPRM).

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Stocks of fnshd gds
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Stocks of Finished Goods sub-index. Tracks inventory buildup at the producer end.
rics.how_to_use: Above 50 = inventory rising (potentially undesired demand weakness or planned stockpiling). Below 50 = inventory falling (strong demand draw). Pair with New Orders — when both fall, downside risk to output near-term.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Stocks of fnshd gds, SA
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Stocks of Finished Goods sub-index, seasonally adjusted.
rics.how_to_use: Cleanest inventory signal. Watch for prolonged elevated readings as production-cut warning; persistent low readings as supply-tightness signal.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Stocks of prchs
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Stocks of Purchases sub-index. Tracks raw-material inventory at producers (input-side stockpile).
rics.how_to_use: Rising stocks of purchases signal manufacturers anticipating production ramp; falling signal de-stocking ahead of expected demand weakness. Used in PMI composite alongside delivery times.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Stocks of prchs, SA
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Stocks of Purchases sub-index, seasonally adjusted.
rics.how_to_use: Use for trend in raw-material inventory accumulation. Surges typically precede production peaks by 1-2 months.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Suppliers' dlvy times
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI: Suppliers' Delivery Times sub-index. Inverted scale: above 50 = lengthening delivery times (supply-chain stress); below 50 = improving delivery times.
rics.how_to_use: Lengthening delivery times correlate with strong demand or supply-chain disruptions. Indonesia's index spiked 2021-22 (global supply-chain shock); normalized post-2023. Watch alongside Input Prices for supply-side stress signals.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Suppliers' dlvy times, SA
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Suppliers' Delivery Times sub-index, seasonally adjusted.
rics.how_to_use: SA version smooths Lebaran-related shipping disruptions. Useful for spotting genuine supply-chain stress vs holiday-driven delivery delays.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Total
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI Headline — composite diffusion index of New Orders, Output, Employment, Suppliers' Delivery Times, and Stocks of Purchases. Survey of ~400 Indonesian manufacturing companies, released first business day of each month at 09:00 WIB.
rics.how_to_use: THE most-watched Indonesia high-frequency activity gauge. Above 50 = manufacturing expanding, below 50 = contracting. Indonesia PMI typically runs 50-54 in expansion (post-2017 average). Sustained sub-50 prints (3+ months) historically signal manufacturing-recession. Surprise vs Reuters consensus drives IDR and JCI same-day.

rics.description: S&P Global, Mfg Sct, Total, SA
rics.meaning: S&P Global Indonesia Manufacturing PMI Headline, seasonally adjusted — the official released headline number markets watch. SA version smooths month-of-Lebaran and Chinese New Year distortions.
rics.how_to_use: The headline release. Same data as aIDPMIT but SA-adjusted — what economists and market commentary cite. Sub-50 readings have correctly preceded Indonesia's small post-2017 manufacturing contractions. Pair with BI's Real Sector Business Activity Survey (aIDBSBACTCR) for the broader business-sentiment picture.
